part_1_frozen_comparison.correct_state: Three models frozen as evidence. V10 and V11 are invalid endpoints. V4 is intermediate but requires pressure-loss decomposition and baseline calibration before use.

part_2_pressure_decomposition.V4_bug_identified: pressure_drop_mmHg was computed as csf_pressure - effective_venous_pressure, which is the DRIVING pressure, not a loss. Checking ≤5mmHg on driving pressure is wrong — higher ΔP is better for drainage.

correct_decomposition.entrance_loss: Loss at shunt inlet from CSF space (minor for straight inlet)
correct_decomposition.friction_loss: Poiseuille friction along shunt length: ΔP_friction = 8μLQ/(πr⁴)
correct_decomposition.curvature_deflection_loss: Loss from deflection/washout geometry: ΔP_deflection = K_deflection × 0.5ρv²
correct_decomposition.mixing_loss: Loss from CSF-venous mixing at outlet: ΔP_mixing = K_mixing × 0.5ρv²
correct_decomposition.outlet_loss: Loss at venous outlet: ΔP_outlet = K_outlet × 0.5ρv²
correct_decomposition.total_loss: ΔP_total_loss = entrance + friction + curvature + mixing + outlet

part_2_pressure_decomposition.which_term_drives_81%_failures: The 81% failures were caused by a METRIC ERROR, not a physical failure. V4 checked 'pressure_drop ≤ 5mmHg' where pressure_drop = driving pressure (ΔP_available). When ΔP_available > 5mmHg (which is GOOD for drainage), the check FAILED. This is backwards — high driving pressure should pass, not fail.
part_2_pressure_decomposition.fix: Replace pressure_drop ≤5mmHg check with: total_geometry_loss < ΔP_available (drainage possible) AND drainage_rate ≥ 80% of target

part_3_eshunt_architecture.assessment: CereVasc patents DO mention valve/flow-control terms: {'valve', 'pressure differential', 'regulat', 'flow rate', 'differential pressure'}. The eShunt likely has a valve or flow-regulation mechanism. This means the Poiseuille-only drainage model is INSUFFICIENT — the valve imposes an additional resistance or threshold that limits drainage to the clinical target of ~0.3 mL/min.
